item.title: Tagging Guideline
item.description:
To keep consistency I created this timeline for myself.

  • Use lowercase, hyphenated tags (tag-name) for consistency.
  • Be specific but not overly granular. Combine broader and narrower tags when useful.
  • Use nouns over verbs where possible.
  • Apply tags based on what the content is about, not just what it mentions.
  • Tags should reflect purpose or recurring patterns, not just one-off references.

item.title: Cause of Divorce (2007–2012)
item.description:
Grindcore from Aachen

I played bass in the grindcore band Cause of Divorce, during 2010 and 2020. We operated somewhere between DIY ethics, blastbeats, and blown-out rehearsal amps. I played around 100 shows across Germany and neighboring countries, sharing stages with lots of underground acts. I paricipated in a couple of releases, some properly pressed, some handmade by myself.

item.title: Ius Talionis (2019–2024)
item.description:
Black Metal from Aachen

I joined Ius Talionis as a bassist in 2019, at a time when the band was undergoing a significant shift — both stylistically and personally. The earlier roots in traditional black metal gave way to darker, more textured influences from the Icelandic and contemporary black metal scenes.

item.title: NecroSlaughter.de (2003–2018)
item.description:
Underground Metal Zine from the Depths of the Internet

NecroSlaughter.de was a DIY webzine focused on the loud, fast, and ugly corners of extreme metal. Over more than a decade, I published hundreds of reviews, interviews, and scene reports — covering everything from obscure grindcore demos to international black and death metal releases.

item.title: TheNocturnalSilence.de (2016–2018)
item.description:
Everything Gloomy – From Dissonant Death to Dark Alternative

The Nocturnal Silence was a digital zine dedicated to the darker shades of underground music — not limited by genre, but bound by atmosphere. The spectrum ranged from dissonant death metal like Infernal Coil to introspective black metal à la Ultha and haunting dark alternative acts like Chelsea Wolfe.

item.title: Docs as Code with AsciiDoc
item.description:
Writing Documentation as Code with AsciiDoc

What is AsciiDoc?

AsciiDoc is a lightweight markup language that allows you to write documentation in plain text. It is designed to be human-readable and supports features like section headers, formatting, tables, links, images, callouts, and much more. AsciiDoc documents can be converted to various output formats such as HTML, PDF, DocBook, and EPUB using tools like Asciidoctor or Pandoc. AsciiDoc can also be included in toolchains like the Maven build tool.

item.title: Taking Notes & Writing Documentation with Markdown
item.description:
Documentation and Note-Taking with Markdown: A Practical Guide

Markdown has become the de facto standard for lightweight text formatting, especially in tech-focused environments. This guide provides an overview of Markdown, its variants, how it compares to AsciiDoc, tools and services that support it, and best practices for writing clean, extensible Markdown documents.

item.title: Bullet Journal (BuJo)
item.description:
Summary

The Bullet Journal (BuJo) is an analog productivity system created by Ryder Carroll. It combines task management, journaling, planning, and note-taking in a minimal, customizable format using pen and paper — or digital equivalents like Markdown.

item.title: IndieWeb
item.description:
Summary

The IndieWeb is a grassroots movement that encourages people to own their online identities and content by publishing on their own websites — rather than relying solely on corporate platforms. It focuses on using open standards, interoperability, and user control.

item.title: Notation of Terraristic Livestock
item.description:
Summary

A consistent notation system for terraristic livestock is essential for managing, documenting, and sharing information on captive animals — especially in private collections, breeding projects, and scientific exchanges.

item.title: Rapid Logging
item.description:
Summary

Rapid Logging is a fast, structured method for capturing notes, tasks, and events using a system of bullets and symbols. It was popularized by the Bullet Journal method developed by Ryder Carroll.

item.title: Semantic Versioning (SemVer)
item.description:
Summary

Semantic Versioning (SemVer) is a versioning scheme for software that conveys meaning about the underlying changes through a structured version number format: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.

item.title: /life
item.description:
Now

  • Homeowner (since 2022): A second-hand house keeps idle hands busy. And the garden? It never sleeps.
  • Gym life: Weightlifting is an office worker’s best defense against back pain.
  • Cats: A clowder with complicated histories — behavioral management meets daily cuteness overload.
  • Centipedes: Misunderstood creatures that deserve more love than they get.
  • Reading: Reading is like weightlifting - but for the mind!
  • Code: The less I code at work, the more I tinker in my free time.

Pets

  • Cats: Lifelong feline companion. Currently serving four furry overlords — the latest joined us as a stray when we bought our house.
  • Centipedes: Keeping and studying these fascinating arthropods since the mid-2000s (with a short break).
  • Previously: Roaches, snakes, a chameleon, spiders, mice — a miniature zoo over the years.

Music

  • Elektronische Körpermusik (2022–2023): Editorial work for a book about EBM.
  • Ius Talionis (2018–2024): Bass duties in a contemporary black metal band.
  • theNocturnalSilence.de (2016–2018): Webzine for black metal and all things gloomy.
  • Cause Of Divorce (2010–2020): Bass in grindcore for the unloved.
  • NecroSlaughter.de (2003–2018): A zine dedicated to death metal and grindcore.

Web Projects

  • scolohub.com (2023–ongoing): A digital resource on centipede husbandry.
  • lycanthropic.de (2016): Web design project.
  • theNocturnalSilence.de (2016–2018): Gloomy music meets HTML.
  • Crypticbrood.de (2015): Web design for a doom-laden trio.
  • NecroSlaughter.de (2003–2018): Where the underground found a voice — and a server.
